chunks: And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Hamdan al-Qalanisi, from Ishaq ibn Bunan, from Ibn Baqqah, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A woman made a claim against her husband during the time of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), saying that he does not have intercourse with her, while he claimed that he does. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ordered her to apply saffron to her private part, and then he would wash his penis. If yellow water came out, he was believed; otherwise, he was ordered to divorce her.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الزَّعْفَرَانِ: saffron (used as a dye for verification)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (AS) resolve disputes over marital consummation in early Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi illustrates the practical application of 'al-istidfar' (using saffron) as a forensic method in early Shia jurisprudence to resolve marital disputes over consummation. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribed that the husband wash his penis with saffron water; if the fluid turned yellow, it confirmed intercourse, whereas its absence justified divorce, reflecting a nuanced approach to evidence in family law.
